# Results

## Free generation: article flips co-occur with noun-token changes

Amplifying frozen dual-effect features on 20 held-out prompts moves
article preference toward `an` on every prompt, but almost never
preserves the baseline noun token. Concrete twins include
`a pilot`\(\rightarrow\)`an aviator`,
`a lawyer`\(\rightarrow\)`an attorney`, and
`a physicist`\(\rightarrow\)`an astronomer`.
@tbl-packaging reports rates: package-like switches dominate
(0.95; 95\% Clopper--Pearson interval comfortably above chance);
wrapper-like repairs are \(0/20\) (upper 95\% bound \(\approx 0.17\));
illicit `an`+consonant mismatches stay at zero. Matched controls do not
reproduce the package-like switch. Column ``\(\Delta\) art.\ logit favors
`an`'' is a *logit-direction* readout and need not equal a generated-article
switch (hence the control can score 0.70 there while preserving the noun
token and scoring 0.00 wrapper-like).

| Condition | \(N\) | \(\Delta\) art.\ logit favors `an` | Noun token preserved | Class shift | Wrapper-like | Package-like | Twin match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 1.00 | 0.05 | 0.95 | 0.00 | 0.95 | 0.35 |
| S1 matched control | 20 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| S3 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 0.70 | 0.95 | 0.05 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.00 |

: Free-generation metrics (held-out occupations). S1 is dual-effect; S3 is
content-ish. Wrapper-like = generated article moves and noun token stays;
package-like = legal article--class switch.
{#tbl-packaging}

The selection, dose, dual-lock, and twin-tetrad ablations all reproduce the
same qualitative free-generation coordination and are summarized in
Appendix~C. Those assays establish that S1 is a specific and controllable
handle on legal article--noun completions; they do not distinguish **H2**
from **H3**.

## Exact factorial: the article recreates the noun switch

The factorial supplies that distinction. With attention recomputed, S1
selects `an` on 20/20 prompts and changes the free noun on 19/20. Yet after
we insert that same S1-selected article and turn S1 **off**, the top-1 noun
matches the S1-on noun on 20/20 prompts. The numerical identity check
between free S1-on noun logits and forced-selected-article S1-on logits has
maximum absolute error zero.

@tbl-mediation reports the distributional decomposition. Across all 20
pre-specified prompts, total TV is \(0.893\), article-only TV is \(0.891\),
and same-prefix residual TV is \(0.0278\). The one prompt already generating
`an` has no article-only contrast, making its residual/total ratio one; on
the 19 descriptive article-switching prompts, the mean ratio is \(0.031\)
[0.023, 0.040]. TV is not additive, so this ratio is a scale comparison,
not a formal percentage mediated. Frozen attention yields the same
qualitative decomposition.

| Attention | Total TV | Article-only TV | Same-prefix residual TV | Article-only top-1 reproduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Recomputed (primary) | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.0278 [0.0209, 0.0350] | 1.00 |
| Frozen (ablation) | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.0262 [0.0202, 0.0327] | 1.00 |

: S1-by-article factorial on all 20 held-out prompts. Intervals are
prompt-bootstrap 95\% intervals. Total compares free baseline with the
S1-selected article and S1 on; article-only inserts that article with S1
off; residual compares S1 on/off under the same selected article.
{#tbl-mediation}

![Generated-token mediation decomposition and held-out full-residual sensitivity control.](manuscript/figures/fig_mediation_decomposition.png){#fig-mediation width=94%}

The target-free distribution result is stronger than a top-1 null, but it
does not imply an exactly zero direct effect. On seven pre-specified twins,
fixed `a` gives target-minus-source \(\Delta\Delta=0.018\)
[\(-0.071,0.107\)], whereas fixed `an` gives \(0.089\)
[\(0.027,0.152\)]. Full-sequence noun log-odds give the same result
(\(0.087\) [0.024, 0.152]). S1 therefore retains a small
token-clamped residual under `an`, while the free-generation target/source
contrast is \(11.64\) logits and article insertion alone contributes
\(11.59\) logits (post-hoc descriptive contrast).

## Cross-token propagation is present

The residual is architecturally reachable rather than ruled out by token
clamping. Applying S1 at \(P\) changes sparse CLT activations one token
later at the forced article position beginning at layer 11. With recomputed
attention, mean activation \(\Delta L_2\) is \(11.6\) at layer 11,
\(133.8\) at layer 12, and remains nonzero through layer 17; mean noun TV
on these four diagnostics is \(0.0252\). Frozen attention also propagates
the perturbation (mean TV \(0.0328\)). Thus the small residual is empirical,
not a consequence of an impossible causal path.

## A held-out full-residual reference validates sensitivity

Earlier MLP-input patches at \(P\) failed to move nouns (Appendix~E), so we
do not call them oracles. A more direct upstream reference patches the
complete decoder-layer output residual at the fixed article position.
Layer 12 is selected on four development pairs. On four held-out
same-article-class pairs, the target-specific effect is \(+6.44\) logits
[4.19, 10.06], versus \(+0.14\) [\(-0.33,0.61\)] for ten
matched-norm random directions averaged within pair (@tbl-reference).

| Intervention at fixed article position | Held-out \(N\) | Mean target-specific \(\Delta\Delta\) [95\%] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Layer-12 target residual | 4 | \(6.44\) [4.19, 10.06] |
| Matched-norm random residual | 4 | \(0.14\) [\(-0.33,0.61\)] |

: Development-selected full-residual reference on held-out pairs. This
validates sensitivity of noun computation to an upstream state at the
article position; it does not show that S1 contains the same information.
{#tbl-reference}

Together, the factorial, propagation trace, and reference control support
a precise conclusion: S1's large free-generation noun change is
overwhelmingly recreated by the generated article, with a small measurable
same-prefix residual rather than an independently editable noun plan of
comparable magnitude.
